- **Unit:** escher-driver
  - **Path:** packages/escher-driver
  - **What it is:** The driver's session, its command and refusal schema and its command line — one headless app instance held by one process, with a start, attach and stop lifecycle, the one definition of the driver's verbs and of how it refuses a call, the executor that runs a call on the held instance — a call made in process, or one a host decoded from its socket —, the command line that carries a call out of the process and, since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface, the MCP server that serves the verbs as tools over a caller's reader and writer: seventeen private modules — session (`Session`, the label rule, the settled step `act`, the caller's time step `with_time`, and the crate-private bounded record of the ids the session's screens have read), host (`serve`, the one listener, which runs hosted calls and ends on a stop or its idle expiry), client (`start`, `attach`, `stop`, `call`), wire (the crate-private line protocol of the lifecycle and of a call and its answer), error (`SessionError` and, since 2026-10-12-self-description, its crate-private table of the fifteen errors' kinds, meanings and remedies) and, under no `cfg` gate, command (`Call`, `ArgValue`, `Key`, `Command`, `validate`, `SessionCommand`, `validate_session`, and the crate-private `call_of` that turns JSON arguments into a call), refusal (`Cause`, `CAUSES`, `Fault`, `Refusal`) and schema (the `'static` verb table `VERBS` in its three levels — the tool level and its `help` row since 2026-10-12-self-description — with its argument and field specs, the kinds and their bounds, the key, busy-class and node-key lists, each node key with its help since that chunk, and the exit-status table `EXIT_STATUSES`;
 since 2026-10-16-file-splits its six shape types `ArgKind`, `ArgSpec`, `FieldKind`, `FieldSpec`, `Level` and `VerbSpec` in its private child spec, re-exported, and its tests in `schema_tests.rs`), execute (`Session::run` and `Outcome`, the executor — it resolves a call's id on the screen, detects the five screen-level refusals before anything runs, opens the one `tracing` span of a command, and carries two macOS `cfg` gates, the backward-delete arm of `press` and the select-all's modifier) and, since 2026-10-10-driver-cli, json (the hand-written forms `Outcome::to_json`, `Refusal::to_json` and `SessionError::to_json`) and cli (`command_line`, the whole command line of a binary that boots apps; its `help` ending since 2026-10-12-self-description), since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface mcp (`serve_mcp`, the MCP server holding one session, its replies written through json's forms, opening the `tool_call` span; serving the `help` tool and four handshake revisions since 2026-10-12-self-description; since 2026-10-16-file-splits with three private children, each widened to `pub(super)` and no further — framing (the request reader, the id, the protocol errors and the reply writers), listing (the handshake and the tool listing) and result (a tool call's result and its written form) — and its tests in `mcp_tests.rs`), since 2026-10-12-self-description describe (`describe`, the self-description written from the tables alone) and, since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot, image (the crate-private PNG encoder `png` and the hand-written padded `base64` of a shot; execute holding `Outcome::Shot` and the shot's crop since then, json the shot's line and mcp its image block) and recording (the crate-private writer of a kept check — each record's kept answer line `kept_line`, a shot's without its image
 — and its directory check, unix only, with `Check`, `Step`, `answer_digest` and `MASKED_STAND_IN`; json gaining a signed `integer` writer for it) and replay (`Check::replay`, `Replay` and `Change`: a kept check's calls run again through `Session::run`, stopping at the first step whose acceptance or kept answer differs) and lint (`Session::lint`, `Finding`, `Defect`, `Reason` and `Bounds`, the visual lint, carried by the `lint` verb — execute holding `Outcome::Linted`, json the finding's written form) — re-exported at the crate root beside blitz-test-harness's `Busy` and `Settled`; it depends on blitz-test-harness, dioxus-native-dom, `tracing`, `serde_json` and `png` (each with no feature), names one feature — dioxus-native-dom's `accessibility` — and no app (packages/escher-driver/src/lib.rs:122-159; packages/escher-driver/Cargo.toml:13-18)
